beats.care: Rising prices are a worry for young people everywhere, including India. This shows how quickly public anger can spill onto the streets.
beats.what: On Saturday, between 5.5 lakh and 8 lakh people marched across France. Masked groups set fires, attacked town halls and looted shops.
beats.why: Protesters, many of them students, are angry about rising living costs and school conditions. The government blamed far-left groups for the violence.

a.body: President Macron said there is no place for violence and looters will pay. The interior minister blamed groups instigated by the far left.
a.label: Government says

b.body: Jean-Luc Mélenchon, who joined the Paris march, said those who share the movement's fight should not loot, and blamed leaders for the chaos.
b.label: Left leader says

cards.note: Far-right leaders also blamed rioters and promised to restore order.
cards.title: Who is to blame for the violence?

cards.body: More than 500 police officers, gendarmes and firefighters were hurt, the interior minister said. Paris police said one person died of a heart attack. In the Paris region alone, 855 people were arrested.
In Limoges, the 19th-century city hall was set on fire and its roof collapsed.

cards.q: Best way to answer price protests?
What started the protests in France?
cards.why: People marched over prices and school conditions; the violence came from smaller groups within the crowds.

hook: Why did a march over *living costs* end with 1,800 arrests in France?

learn.t: Police counted about 5.5 lakh marchers; organisers said about 8 lakh. Most protests were peaceful.

sources.name: CBS News (AP)
sources.title: French police arrest more than 1,800 people after violent protests erupt across country

sources.name: Euronews
sources.title: France reels after cost-of-living protests see widespread violence

tldr: Hundreds of thousands marched across France against rising living costs; violence broke out in several cities and at least 1,800 people were arrested.
watch: France votes for a new president next spring. Watch whether the government offers cost-of-living relief.
